summary: Identified critical command injection and path traversal vulnerabilities in file management operations.

findings.title: Command injection vulnerability in archive()
findings.body: The `archive` function interpolates the unvalidated `name` argument directly into a shell command string executed via `execSync`. Passing inputs containing shell metacharacters allows arbitrary command execution, and filenames with spaces will cause command execution failures.
findings.recommendation: Use `execFileSync` or `spawnSync` with an arguments array rather than shell string interpolation, and validate `name`.

findings.title: Path traversal vulnerability in readUpload()
findings.body: The `readUpload` function constructs target paths with `path.join(ROOT, name)` without validating that the resolved path stays within the `ROOT` directory. An attacker can supply relative path sequences (e.g., `../`) to read arbitrary files from the filesystem.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the path using `path.resolve` and assert that the target path starts with the resolved `ROOT` directory path.

samples.summary: Identified critical security vulnerabilities and reliability issues in src/files.js, including command injection, path traversal, and unvalidated property access.

findings.title: Command injection via unescaped input in child_process.execSync
findings.body: In src/files.js, archive concatenates the unvalidated name argument directly into a shell command executed via execSync. An attacker providing command separators (e.g. ';', '&&', or '$()') can execute arbitrary commands on the host system.
findings.recommendation: Use execFileSync or spawnSync with an argument array rather than string interpolation in a shell: execFileSync('tar', ['-czf', `${name}.tar.gz`, path.join(ROOT, name)]).

findings.title: Path traversal allowing arbitrary file read
findings.body: In src/files.js, readUpload resolves file paths using path.join(ROOT, name) without verifying that the resolved path stays within ROOT. Supplying relative path segments like '../' allows reading arbitrary files across the filesystem.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the path and ensure it is contained within ROOT (e.g. const resolved = path.resolve(ROOT, name); if (!resolved.startsWith(path.resolve(ROOT) + path.sep)) throw new Error('Access denied');) or restrict name using path.basename(name).

findings.title: Unsafe property access and missing boundary validation in pickPage
findings.body: In src/files.js, pickPage accesses body.page without verifying that body is defined, leading to potential unhandled TypeErrors. Furthermore, parseInt is called without a radix, and the parsed page index is not validated against the bounds of the pages array.
findings.recommendation: Ensure body is defined, parse with a radix (parseInt(body?.page, 10)), and verify that the index is a non-negative integer within Array.isArray(pages) and page < pages.length before indexing.

samples.summary: Critical command injection, high-severity path traversal, and unvalidated input handling vulnerabilities identified in src/files.js.

findings.title: Command injection vulnerability in archive
findings.body: The `archive` function directly interpolates the unvalidated `name` parameter into a shell command string passed to `execSync`. An attacker can supply shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands on the system.
findings.recommendation: Replace `execSync` with `execFileSync` or `spawnSync` using an argument array (e.g., `execFileSync('tar', ['-czf', `${name}.tar.gz`, targetPath])`) and sanitize the input filename.

findings.title: Path traversal vulnerability in readUpload and archive
findings.body: `readUpload` and `archive` use `path.join(ROOT, name)` without validating that the resulting path is strictly confined to the `/srv/uploads` root directory. An attacker can supply relative path segments (e.g., `../../etc/passwd`) to access arbitrary files on the filesystem.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the target path using `path.resolve` and verify that it starts with the resolved `ROOT` path, or restrict input to `path.basename(name)`.

findings.title: Missing null check and bounds validation in pickPage
findings.body: `pickPage` accesses `body.page` without checking if `body` is defined, and parses `body.page` without an explicit radix or bounds check against `pages.length`. This can cause uncaught `TypeError` or unexpected `undefined` index accesses.
findings.recommendation: Validate that `body` is an object, parse `body.page` with `Number.parseInt(body.page, 10)`, and ensure the parsed integer is non-negative and within `pages` array bounds.
